**Step 1: Monthly payment formula**

For a fully amortized loan:
\[
\text{PMT}=P\frac{r(1+r)^n}{(1+r)^n-1}
\]
Total cost of borrowing = \(n \times \text{PMT} - P + \text{fee}\)

**Loan A**
- \(P=20{,}000,\ r=0.049/12=0.0040833,\ n=72,\ \text{fee}=0\)
- \((1+r)^n \approx 1.340981\)
- \(\text{PMT} \approx 20{,}000 \times \frac{0.0040833 \times 1.340981}{0.340981} \approx \$321.17\)
- Total interest \(\approx 72(321.17)-20{,}000 \approx \$3{,}124.37\)
- **Total cost \(\approx \$3{,}124.37\)**

**Loan B**
- \(P=20{,}000,\ r=0.069/12=0.00575,\ n=72,\ \text{fee}=1\%\times20{,}000=\$200\)
- \((1+r)^n \approx 1.511064\)
- \(\text{PMT} \approx \$340.02\)
- Total interest \(\approx 72(340.02)-20{,}000 \approx \$4{,}481.48\)
- **Total cost \(\approx \$4{,}481.48 + 200 = \$4{,}681.48\)**

**Loan C**
- \(P=20{,}000,\ r=0.049/12=0.0040833,\ n=60,\ \text{fee}=2\%\times20{,}000=\$400\)
- \((1+r)^n \approx 1.276984\)
- \(\text{PMT} \approx \$376.51\)
- Total interest \(\approx 60(376.51)-20{,}000 \approx \$2{,}590.55\)
- **Total cost \(\approx \$2{,}590.55 + 400 = \$2{,}990.55\)**

Loan C has the lowest total cost, despite its upfront fee, because the shorter 5-year term saves more interest than the fee adds.
